doc.title: Ray Ricker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 27, 2022

chapter: Denver youth and University of Denver
title: First jazz records: Horace Silver and the Columbia Record Archive
summary: His first jazz record was a Horace Silver EP, then a Columbia record club collection with Miles Davis and Monk.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: If you had gone out to a record store about that time when you were playing the hockey rink gig, what might you have purchased as far as non-classical music?

Non-classical. I remember pretty much my first one I got was a ten inch 33-1/3 — no a ten — or it was the small one, not the — maybe the big one was the ten inch. I don’t know. But this was the smaller one. And it was Horace Silver. And it had four tunes on it you know. And that was the first one I got. After that I joined the Columbia Record Archive you know, the whatever, the one where you got a record every month and they just came. And sometimes you got to choose you know. But there were a lot of guys that recorded for Columbia like Miles Davis and Thelonious Monk, and that kind of thing. So I built a record collection that way.
